plain.li: [faith:minority] Those of us who keep a different ideoligion would like an evening of our own, just once.
[faith:alone] I'm the only one here who keeps my ideoligion, and an evening for it would mean a lot to me.
[trait:Kind] Nobody should feel like a guest in their own home because of what they believe.
Ten days of treating every ideoligion alike is a small thing to ask of the council.

blunt.li: Not everyone here keeps the colony's ideoligion, and the council should act like it knows that.

cheerful.li: An evening of someone else's faith sounds like a good evening to me.

plain.li: [devout] The colony's ideoligion has kept us together, and the council shouldn't set it aside for ten days.
[faith:majority] Most of us keep the colony's ideoligion, and the council should remember that.
I don't see why the council should hold an evening for an ideoligion that isn't the colony's.
[faith:devout] The council is meant to stand by the colony's ideoligion, not treat it as one among many.

warm.li: I don't mind what other people believe, but I'd rather the council didn't make a decree of it.

cold.li: The devout will trust the council less for this, and the council needs them.

plain.li: [skill:Plants] There's food ripening out there that nobody planted, and I'd like to go and pick it.
[trait:Ascetic] Whatever grows wild out there is good enough food for me.
[tribal] Our people always kept the berry days, and this is the time for them.
[medieval] Let's glean the hedges while there's still something in them to glean.
[industrial|spacer] It's worth surveying what the land grows for us before it rots where it stands.

cheerful.li: A few days out with a basket sounds good to me.

plain.li: [trait:Undergrounder] I'd rather be under a roof than wandering about looking for berries.
[trait:Industrious] Picking berries one at a time is a poor use of a day's work.
Six mornings of the growers wandering off, and the crops will suffer for it.
We planted fields so we wouldn't have to go looking for food.

warm.li: I'd rather the growers spent their days in the fields with the rest of us.

cold.li: A basket of berries won't feed us through the winter.

plain.li: [trait:Ascetic] Nobody needs the lamps burning while they sleep.
[trait:Undergrounder] A dark room at night is how it should be anyway.
The batteries run low before morning, and the lamps are the easiest place to save.
[industrial] Lights out at eleven means the batteries will still have something in them at dawn.
[spacer] Dimming the lamps at night costs us nothing but a little light.

cheerful.li: I sleep better in the dark anyway, so this suits me fine.

plain.li: [trait:NightOwl] Night is when I'm up and about, and I can't see what I'm doing without a lamp.
[trait:Nervous|trait:Volatile] I don't like waking up in the dark and not being able to see the door.
Somebody will walk into a wall in the dark before the five nights are out.
[afterraid] Raiders were just here, and now we're turning the lights off at night?

warm.li: I'd rather nobody here had to wake up frightened in the dark.

blunt.li: Build more batteries and leave the lamps alone.

plain.li: [trait:Industrious|trait:HardWorker] Give me a week of felling and the woodpile will be up to the roof.
[trait:Tough] A week of felling in the cold never did me any harm.
[lowtech] The nights are getting longer, and the fires will need feeding every one of them.
Wood is easy to get now and hard to get once the snow comes, so let's fell it.
[winter] It's cold already, and the woodpile is lower than it should be.

warm.li: I'd like everyone to have a warm room this winter, and that means cutting wood now.

plain.li: [trait:Lazy|trait:Slothful] Eight days of carrying logs, and my back aches just thinking about it.
The woodpile will do us, and eight days is a long time to spend on it.
I like having trees around the colony, and this will clear a lot of them.
[hurt] I'm in no shape for felling, and somebody will still expect me to haul.

blunt.li: Cut what we need when we need it, not eight days of it at once.

cold.li: The cutters will be no use for anything else for a week.

plain.li: [faith:devout] Our ideoligion has carried this colony this far, and it should have the council's word behind it.
[devout] Every meeting opening with a word from the faith is how it should have been all along.
[faith:majority] Most of us pray the same way, and naming it the colony's would settle a lot of arguments.
One ideoligion for the colony means one set of holy days, and fewer quarrels about which to keep.

blunt.li: Name it the colony's ideoligion and be done with it.

cheerful.li: Hearing a word from the faith at every meeting would put people in a better mood.

plain.li: [faith:minority] Those of us who keep another ideoligion will feel like guests in our own colony.
[faith:alone] I'm the only one here who keeps my ideoligion, and this tells me how much that counts.
People should come to an ideoligion because they want to, not because the council named it.
[devout] I won't be talked out of my own ideoligion by a decree.

warm.li: I'd rather we got along with our different ideoligions than had one named for us.

cheerful.li: Name an ideoligion if you like, but I'll be keeping my own, thank you.

plain.li: [trait:Kind] I don't like the idea of the animals being chased down every morning for six days.
[tribal] Our people never hunted more than the camp could eat, and this is more.
If the hunters are out every morning, who's going to do their other work?
[spacer] A cull sounds tidy until you're the one dragging the carcasses back.

blunt.li: Animals fight back, and I'd rather not be patching up hunters all week.

cold.li: Six days of hunting now leaves fewer animals for next year.

plain.li: [trait:Industrious] I'm not tired, and I don't see why the work should slow down for three days.
[trait:HardWorker] There's too much waiting to be done for three slow days.
[fall] The harvest won't wait three days for us to feel better.
If we slow down now, the stores will be the first thing to feel it.

warm.li: I know people are tired, but I'm worried about what falls behind while we rest.

gloomy.li: Three easy days, and then three hard ones catching up.
